sections.text:
1 [Eleutherius ille praeceptor Iohannis Abrami idem esse videtur atque astrologus
Eleus huius nominis qui Mytilenis anno 1388 p. C. n. codicem Angelicanum 29
descripsit (Studi Italiani, t. IV, [1896], p. 64). Nam et similiter magister atque
discipulus expleto opere Deo gratias egerunt : τῷ συντελεστῇ τῶν καλῶν θεῷ
χάρις (Cod. Ang., f. 152). — F. C.]
sections.en: 1 [That Eleutherius, teacher of Iohannes Abramus, seems to be the same as the Elean astrologer of this name who copied the Codex Angelicanus 29 at Mytilene in the year 1388 A.D. (Studi Italiani, vol. IV, [1896], p. 64). For similarly both master and disciple gave thanks to God when the work was completed: τῷ συντελεστῇ τῶν καλῶν θεῷ χάρις ('thanks to God the accomplisher of good things') (Cod. Ang., f. 152). - F. C.]

summary.headline: Codex 16: Abramios Astrological Collection
summary.text: Description of Florentine codex 16 (Plut. 28), a 14th-century manuscript copied by John Abramios, with a 265-chapter index, Abramios’s verses, astrological traditions, Demetrios Chloros’s method for finding the horoscopos, thematia, solar ingress calculations, star material, and methods for determining terrestrial clime.
